summary: Same family (a centred N-armed star/pinwheel on the grid, with matching Size, InitialColor, ColorSpeed and arm-count-selector laws), but the port draws a permanently over-wound, low-contrast multi-turn spiral instead of the original's crisp straight-to-lightly-twirled arms, runs its rotation ~10x too slow with an almost dead TwistSpeed, gives StarRotation a bipolar mapping the original does not have, and looks nothing like the original at untouched defaults.
observations: CONTROL-SURFACE MISMATCH: the original's first slider is named `sliderSize` (label "Size"); the port names it `sliderStarSize` (label "StarSize"). All other seven control names/kinds/labels match exactly (sliderLineWidth, sliderTwistSpeed, sliderRotationSpeed, sliderInitialColor, sliderColorSpeed, sliderArms, sliderStarRotation — all `slider`). Both sides compile with no runtime error; neither binds sensors (wantsSensors false on both).

UNTOUCHED DEFAULTS ARE COMPLETELY DIFFERENT. Original (16x16 grid, and confirmed at 48x48): a SOLID, flat-filled 6-pointed star, one uniform hue per frame, that BLINKS on/off at ~7.7 Hz (200 fps stats: ~26-frame on/off cycle = 0.13 s, ~60% duty, meanBrightness swinging 0..12 every cycle) while its hue races round the wheel at ~243 deg/s (full colour wheel every ~1.5 s). Baseline statsSummary: motion avg 6.9, motionLit avg 50.9, brightnessTrend `volatile`, zeroMotionFrames 3/120. Port: a flat GREEN 5-armed spiral pinwheel plus a few detached blocks, no blinking at all (meanBrightness pinned 5..8, brightnessTrend `steady`), motion avg 0.2, motionLit avg 1.7, zeroMotionFrames 102/120, and a hue that walks at only ~2.1 deg/s (full wheel ~170 s, measured over the 240 s survey). So untouched the original's hue is ~115x faster and it strobes; the port is a slow, steady green spiral.

Untouched-default color speed on the original sits OUTSIDE the ColorSpeed slider's range (243 deg/s untouched vs 6 deg/s at ColorSpeed=1) — a property of the pattern, not an analysis artefact. The port's untouched 2.1 deg/s sits below its own ColorSpeed=0.5 setting.

STRUCTURE AT MATCHED DIALS (48x48 grid, Size=0.7, LineWidth=0.5, InitialColor=0.3, ColorSpeed=0, all speeds neutralised at each side's own zero): original draws N crisp radial petals with deep black gaps between them — angular-DFT contrast (fundamental amplitude / DC) 0.61 at arms<=0.3 (1 arm), 0.61 at arms 0.4-0.6 (2 arms), 0.63 at arms>=0.7 (3 arms). Port draws the same fundamental arm count but wound into many tight spiral turns, so its angular contrast collapses to 0.27 / 0.08 / 0.04 for the same three bands — i.e. the port's arms are 2-15x lower contrast and read as a smeared spiral rather than a star.

ARMS SELECTOR MATCHES. Fine sweep at 0.1 steps: both sides quantise sliderArms into exactly the same three bands — [0.0-0.3] -> 1 arm, [0.4-0.6] -> 2 arms, [0.7-1.0] -> 3 arms (dominant angular harmonic k=1/2/3 on both sides in the inner annulus r=3..14).

The 6-pointed OUTER STAR SILHOUETTE is present on both sides (dominant outer-annulus harmonic k=6, contrast 0.81 orig / 0.49 port at arms<=0.6), so the 'star' half of the pattern is at least qualitatively ported.

TWIST IS THE HEADLINE STRUCTURAL BUG: with sliderTwistSpeed=0 (and rotation neutral) the ORIGINAL is a perfectly straight-rayed star (three sharp diamond petals, zero curvature) and is byte-frozen (motionLit avg 0.00 over 4 s). The PORT at the identical settings is already a tightly-wound 7-turn spiral — it carries a large constant twist offset that no dial value removes. Sweeping TwistSpeed 0->1 the original winds and unwinds its petals into a swirl and back (a visible 'twirl' oscillation, motionLit 0.01 -> 29.93, monotone); the port's shape barely changes (motionLit 0.00 -> 3.09, ~10x weaker, and the sheet at TwistSpeed=1 is visually the same tight spiral throughout 4 s).

ROTATION SPEED ~10x TOO SLOW. At sliderRotationSpeed=1 (StarRotation=0.5 = both sides' zero, TwistSpeed=0, arms=0.8), unwrapped k=3 angular-phase tracking at 0.01 s spacing gives the ORIGINAL -377.7 deg/s (about 1.05 revolutions per second; the 20 fps filmstrip shows ~19 deg of rotation per frame). The PORT's inner spiral (k=3, annuli r=4-10 and r=6-14, tracked over 6 s at 0.1 s spacing) turns at -36.0 / -36.3 deg/s — same direction, 10.4x slower; its 0.55 s filmstrip looks essentially frozen.

ROTATION DIAL RESPONSE CURVE DIFFERS IN SHAPE. motionLit avg vs sliderRotationSpeed (0/0.125/.../1): orig 0.01, 8.86, 16.03, 21.75, 26.19, 29.72, 33.09, 36.22, 38.94 (steep then saturating/concave); port 0.00, 0.87, 1.77, 2.58, 3.41, 4.22, 5.02, 5.81, 6.57 (perfectly linear, ~6x smaller even before accounting for motion saturation). Same for TwistSpeed: orig 0.01, 6.75, 12.10, 16.22, 19.69, 22.77, 25.27, 27.73, 29.93 (concave); port 0.00, 0.02, 0.21, 0.46, 0.82, 1.26, 1.82, 2.40, 3.09 (convex/quadratic, ~10x smaller).

STARROTATION MAPPING IS WRONG-SHAPED. Fine sweep (motionLit avg): original is ONE-SIDED — 0.00 for every value <= 0.5, then 0.73 / 10.58 / 31.01 / 44.93 at 0.625/0.75/0.875/1. Port is BIPOLAR and symmetric about 0.5 — 14.27 / 7.22 / 3.10 / 1.01 / 0.00 / 0.97 / 3.08 / 7.21 / 14.29 across 0..1. Consequences: (a) the port spins at full speed where the original is dead still (StarRotation 0 to 0.375); (b) the port's peak star-rotation rate is 3.1x weaker than the original's (14.3 vs 44.9 motionLit).

COLORSPEED MATCHES WELL. With rotation frozen, mean hue advanced 60 deg over 20 s (3.0 deg/s) on BOTH sides at ColorSpeed=0.5, and ~121 deg over 20 s (6.0 deg/s) on both at ColorSpeed=1; both are hue-static at ColorSpeed=0. INITIALCOLOR matches essentially exactly: hue 139 (orig) vs 140 (port) at v=0 and v=1, 319 vs 320 at v=0.5 — the mapping including its wrap is identical.

SIZE / STARSIZE MATCH IN DIRECTION AND ROUGH MAGNITUDE: mean brightness 0/6/12 (orig) vs 1/8/14 (port) at v=0/0.5/1; v=0 blanks the figure on both. LINEWIDTH also matches in direction (thin petals -> fat wedges on the orig; thin -> thick spiral arms on the port): mean 7/9/12 orig vs 10/11/14 port.

SPEED RATIO AT ALL-DIALS-0.5 (16x16, shape-only autocorrelation on per-pixel max-channel, 0.1 s lag resolution over 15 s): the ORIGINAL's figure repeats with a sharp period of 1.95 s (corr peaks 0.86/0.96/0.90/0.92/0.93 at lags 1.95, 3.9, 5.9, 7.8, 9.8 s, ~0.48 between peaks); the PORT decorrelates smoothly to a minimum of 0.10 at 2.4 s and only recovers to a broad 0.70 at 4.85 s — 2.5x slower and with no crisp periodicity.

COLOR STRUCTURE ACROSS THE FIGURE differs at speed-dialed settings: at all-dials-0.5 on 48x48 the original's petals carry several distinct hues at once (green / magenta / blue / yellow in one frame, a rainbow sweep along and between arms) while the port renders the whole figure in one hue (magenta drifting to orange over 12 s). Per-frame circular hue spread is similar numerically (0.06-0.13 both sides) but the original's MEAN hue sweeps 319->59->150->231->320 deg in 2.0 s (rotation-driven, since ColorSpeed alone accounts for only 3 deg/s) whereas the port's mean hue moves 314->335 deg over 5.5 s.

NEITHER SIDE IS FRAME-RATE COUPLED: the original's untouched brightness period is 13 frames at 20 fps and 26 frames at 40 fps — both 0.65 s (the 10 fps survey aliases it to a false 1.3 s). Rendering at 10/20/40/100/200 fps changes neither side's per-second behaviour.
BOTH SIDES ARE RESOLUTION-INDEPENDENT: the same logical figure is drawn on 16x16 and 48x48, just finer. Not a divergence axis here.

BOTH SIDES ARE SEED-INDEPENDENT (seed 1234 reproduces seed 1's stats byte-for-byte) and both have a stable steady state: at --skip 120 (12 s at 20 fps) and over --seconds 30 --fps 4 the original still posts motion 5-8 and the port motion 0-2, i.e. neither dies, but the port stays near-static throughout.

SURVEY REGIMES: neither side has mode rotation. Over 240 s the only slow structure is the hue walk (port ~170 s per full wheel, original racing far faster); the port's figure also breathes slowly between a tight spiral and a straighter cross around t=65 s. A --skip 120 re-render confirms the late window is the same behaviour as the early one on both sides.

PROBE FALSE-INERT CAUGHT: --probe-controls reported the ORIGINAL's sliderTwistSpeed as inert (maxDelta exactly 0.00 at 0/0.5/1). That is a setter-interaction artefact — with the other seven controls explicitly pinned, TwistSpeed is one of the original's strongest dials (motionLit 0.01 -> 29.93). All 16 controls (8 per side) were verified live by manual sweep.

dials.name: sliderSize / sliderStarSize
dials.origEffect: Scales the whole star; v=0 blanks the rig (mean brightness 0), v=0.5 mean 6, v=1 mean 12 and the petals reach the grid edge.
dials.portEffect: Same law and direction: v=0 near-black (mean 1), v=0.5 mean 8, v=1 mean 14, spiral fills the grid.

dials.name: sliderLineWidth
dials.origEffect: Fattens the radial petals from thin diamonds (mean 7) to broad wedges (mean 12) without changing their count or straightness.
dials.portEffect: Fattens the spiral arms over the same range (mean 10 -> 14); direction and magnitude match, but it is thickening a spiral rather than a straight ray.

dials.name: sliderTwistSpeed
dials.origEffect: Primary 'twirl' dial and a true speed: v=0 freezes the figure completely (motionLit 0.00) with perfectly straight arms; raising it winds and unwinds the petals into a swirl and back, motionLit rising concavely to 29.93 at v=1.
dials.portEffect: Almost dead. motionLit 0.00 / 0.02 / 0.21 / 0.46 / 0.82 / 1.26 / 1.82 / 2.40 / 3.09 across 0..1 (~10x weaker, convex not concave), and the arms are already fully over-wound at v=0 so no winding/unwinding is visible in a 4 s window.

dials.name: sliderRotationSpeed
dials.origEffect: Spins the whole figure. v=0 frozen; v=1 = -377.7 deg/s (~1.05 rev/s). motionLit 0.01 -> 38.94, concave (fast rise then saturating).
dials.portEffect: Spins in the same direction but 10.4x slower: v=1 = -36.2 deg/s. motionLit 0.00 -> 6.57 and perfectly linear in the dial rather than concave.

dials.name: sliderInitialColor
dials.origEffect: Sets the base hue; hue 139 deg at v=0, 319 deg at v=0.5, 139 deg again at v=1 (one full wrap across the slider).

dials.name: sliderColorSpeed
dials.origEffect: Hue-walk rate: static at v=0, 3.0 deg/s at v=0.5, 6.0 deg/s at v=1 (measured over 20 s with rotation frozen).
dials.portEffect: Identical: static at 0, 3.0 deg/s at 0.5, 6.0 deg/s at 1.

dials.name: sliderArms
dials.origEffect: Three-band selector for the arm count: [0-0.3] = 1 arm, [0.4-0.6] = 2 arms, [0.7-1] = 3 arms, with high angular contrast (fundamental/DC 0.61-0.63) in every band.
dials.portEffect: Same three bands and same fundamental arm counts (1/2/3), but the arms are wound into many turns so the angular contrast collapses to 0.27 / 0.08 / 0.04 — visually it reads as a 3-, 5- and 7-arm tight spiral rather than a 1-, 2- and 3-pointed star.

dials.name: sliderStarRotation
dials.origEffect: One-sided speed dial: dead flat (motionLit 0.00) for every value <= 0.5, then rising steeply — 0.73 / 10.58 / 31.01 / 44.93 at 0.625 / 0.75 / 0.875 / 1.
dials.portEffect: Bipolar V about 0.5: 14.27 / 7.22 / 3.10 / 1.01 / 0.00 / 0.97 / 3.08 / 7.21 / 14.29 across 0..1. So the port spins hard where the original is still, and its maximum rate is 3.1x weaker than the original's.

feedback: Rename the port's `sliderStarSize` back to `sliderSize` (label "Size") — the original's control list is authoritative and every other name/label/kind already matches.

BIGGEST FIX — remove the constant twist offset. With sliderTwistSpeed=0 and rotation neutral, the original draws perfectly STRAIGHT radial petals and is completely frozen; the port draws a 7-turn tight spiral at those same settings. The port's radius-dependent angular offset must go to exactly zero when the twist term is zero, so that twist accumulates only from TwistSpeed*time. Target for a check: at Size=0.7, LineWidth=0.5, Arms=0.8, TwistSpeed=0, RotationSpeed=0, StarRotation=0.5, the port should render three straight, sharply separated petals with an inner-annulus (r=3..14) angular fundamental/DC contrast near 0.63 — it currently measures 0.04.

Restore the twirl animation amplitude. Sweeping TwistSpeed 0->1 should take motionLit from 0.00 to ~30 (48x48, 10 fps, 4 s window) with a concave curve; the port currently reaches only 3.09 and rises convexly. Visually the original's petals must visibly wind up into a swirl and unwind again inside a few seconds — the port's shape barely changes over 4 s.

Speed the rotation up by ~10x. At sliderRotationSpeed=1 the original turns at -377.7 deg/s (roughly one revolution per second, ~19 deg per frame at 20 fps); the port turns at -36.2 deg/s. The direction is already correct — only the scale is wrong. Also note the original's rate-vs-dial curve is concave (steep at the bottom, saturating near the top) while the port's is exactly linear, so a pure gain change will still leave the low end too slow relative to the original.

Make sliderStarRotation one-sided, not bipolar. The original is completely still for every value from 0 to 0.5 and then accelerates steeply (motionLit 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0.01 / 0.73 / 10.58 / 31.01 / 44.93 at 0, 0.125, ..., 1). The port instead treats 0.5 as the stop point and mirrors the speed either side of it, so it is spinning at full rate at StarRotation=0 where the original is frozen. Its peak rate is also ~3.1x too low (14.3 vs 44.9 motionLit).

Reproduce the untouched-default look, which is currently unrecognisable. Untouched, the original is a SOLID flat-filled 6-pointed star that BLINKS on and off at ~7.7 Hz (~0.13 s cycle, ~60% duty, whole-rig mean brightness dropping to exactly 0 between flashes) while its single flat hue races at ~243 deg/s (full colour wheel every ~1.5 s). The port untouched is a steady, non-blinking green 5-arm spiral whose hue crawls at ~2.1 deg/s (full wheel ~170 s). Note the original's untouched hue rate is ~40x FASTER than anything its own ColorSpeed slider reaches (6 deg/s at v=1), so the untouched internal defaults are out of the slider's range — the port must set the same out-of-range initial values, not a mid-slider value.

Do NOT touch InitialColor, ColorSpeed, Size or the Arms band boundaries — all four already match the original to within measurement noise (InitialColor hue 139/319/139 vs 140/320/140; ColorSpeed 0 / 3.0 / 6.0 deg/s on both sides; Arms quantised into the same [0-0.3]/[0.4-0.6]/[0.7-1] bands giving 1/2/3 arms on both).

Secondary: at speed-dialed settings the original's figure carries several hues at once across its arms (a rainbow sweep along and between petals, mean hue sweeping a full wheel in ~2.0 s as it spins), while the port paints the whole figure one hue at a time. Some of this will come back for free once the rotation is 10x faster, but check whether the hue term should also be a function of angle/radius and not only of time.
Neither side is frame-rate coupled and neither is seed-dependent, so no work is needed there; verify any fix at 20 fps and confirm it holds at 10 and 40 fps.
